data.author: Imran Mulla

Submitted by

on

As storms batter Gaza, 150,000 tents in aid lorries remain stuck outside the Palestinian enclave
Humanitarian aid trucks at the Rafah border crossing with the Gaza Strip on 4 February 2026 (AFP)
Off
More than 50 British MPs are supporting a parliamentary motion calling on their government to take "urgent action" on getting aid into Gaza and demanding fresh sanctions on Israel.
The motion, which was tabled on Tuesday night by Labour MP Richard Burgon, notes "UN reports that tens of thousands of already displaced families have suffered damage to their shelters" in Gaza.
It says this has "been made far worse by Israel's widespread destruction of homes, drainage systems and other essential infrastructure that have left most Palestinians in Gaza displaced".
The motion further condemns "Israel's ongoing restrictions on the entry of humanitarian aid, including materials needed to provide shelter, respond to flooding, and aid reconstruction", as well as its "restrictions on bringing humanitarian supplies and international staff into Gaza".
Some 65 percent of Gaza’s population, about 1.4 million people, live in tents or makeshift shelters, according to the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (Ocha).
In the last week, torrential rainfall and deadly storms have flooded or destroyed tens of thousands of these tents.
Israel continues to bar aid groups from bringing supplies and international staff into the territory. The Norwegian Refugee Council reported last month that Israeli authorities were allowing just 15 trucks carrying items Israel considers to be "dual-use" into Gaza from Jordan once a week.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israel hands over body of Palestinian teen who died in custody
data.author: Katherine Hearst
data.summary:
Israel hands over body of Palestinian teen who died in custody
The Israeli authorities have handed over the body of 17-year-old Palestinian detainee Walid Khaled Ahmad, who died in March 2025 while held in Megiddo Prison after six months of detention, Wafa reports.
Ahmad died after he had been starved and denied medical treatment, according to the report.
His body was released following legal efforts by Nadia Daqa, a lawyer with the Commission of Detainees and Ex-Detainees Affairs.
Testimonies collected by Defence for Children International indicate that he became dizzy and collapsed on 22 March 2025. Fellow detainees said they called for help, but guards did not respond. They said they carried him to the yard gate, where guards eventually took him away.
In December 2025 an Israeli court in Hadera closed the investigation into his death, claiming all avenues had been exhausted, despite finding indications he had been starved.
Israeli authorities continue to withhold the bodies of 98 Palestinian prisoners who have died in custody since 1967.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Gideon Saar warns 'attempts to harm Israel also harm Britain' after meeting UK Conservative delegation
data.author: Katherine Hearst
data.summary:
Gideon Saar warns 'attempts to harm Israel also harm Britain' after meeting UK Conservative delegation
Israel's Minister of Foreign Affairs Gideon Saar has said that UK-Israeli relations have been "damaged" following a "series of unilateral anti-Israel measures pursued by the Labour government since 2024".
Saar made the comments following a meeting with a visting delegation from the British Conservative Party on Wednesday evening in Jerusalem.
In a post on X, he said he had briefed the group "on the strategic challenges facing Israel, including the ongoing, systematic and openly declared attempt by Iran and its allies to destroy it".
But he warned that the relationship between Israel and the UK has been damaged "against our wishes", and said that "attempts to harm Israel also harm Britain itself".
I was pleased to meet this evening in Jerusalem with a visiting delegation from the British Conservative Party, led by Party Chairman Kevin Hollinrake. I briefed our friends on the strategic challenges facing Israel, including the ongoing, systematic and openly declared attempt by Iran and its allies to destroy it. The relationship between Israel and Britain is important to both countries. Unfortunately, it has been damaged, against our wishes, by a series of unilateral anti-Israel measures pursued by the Labour government since 2024. As attorneys general from 13 U.S. states recently warned, attempts to harm Israel also harm Britain itself. Irish lawmakers are calling for an investigation into Ireland's data regulator over concerns that Microsoft's data centre campus outside Dublin hosts an app used by Israel to control the movements of Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza.
Last year, rights groups EKO and the Irish Centre for Civil Liberties (ICCL) filed a complaint with Ireland’s Data Protection Commission (DPC), raising concerns that Microsoft’s Grange Castle data centre was hosting elements of the Almunasseq app, used by the Israeli army to monitor Palestinians.
The DPC has still not given a definitive response to the rights groups over the status of the complaint.
Sinead Gibney, who serves in the Dail Eireann, the Irish parliament's lower house, said Microsoft's Irish data centres are "fuelling the crime of apartheid against Palestinians" in the West Bank and Gaza.
“Microsoft must be held accountable and I’ll be pushing for the Department of Enterprise to fully investigate this matter in light of the wealth of UN reports detailing the apartheid system," she told Middle East Eye.
"I'm calling on Microsoft to explain why it’s providing the Israeli government with the tools and technologies to sustain its system of apartheid – a system under which millions of Palestinians are being denied basic human rights."
The complaint was submitted on behalf of a Palestinian resident of Gaza and the West Bank, as well as a European Union citizen, based on evidence provided by a whistleblower.
Evidence seen by MEE and gathered by EKO and the ICCL showed that Israel used Microsoft’s Azure cloud computing platform to host elements of the Almunasseq app.

Six political parties in the Dutch city of Tilburg have condemned a local arms company’s deal with Israeli gunmaker Israel Weapon Industries (IWI).
The parties have asked the municipal authorities whether they can prevent weapons produced under the agreement from reaching Israel’s military and whether they can block local production.
Tilburg-based AIA bought designs and technical know-how from IWI and plans to make rifles and light machine guns at an industrial park in the city.
The agreement covers the Arad 5 infantry rifle and the Negev UX light machine gun. Production will initially take place in Tilburg before moving to a larger site in Overijssel, according to Dutch broadcaster Omroep Brabant.

data.author: Alex MacDonald

Turkey's oldest LGBTQ+ group has office closed as crackdown continues
Submitted by

on

Lambda Istanbul said closure by authorities aimed to 'isolate' LGBTQ+ people and deprive them of a space to organise
Participants in the 12th Trans Pride March in Kadikoy, Istanbul on 21 June 2026 (Abdullah Tepeli/Zuma Press Wire)
Off
Authorities in Turkey have closed the office of the country's oldest LGBTQ+ organisation, claiming it is an "unauthorised social club".
The Istanbul Governor’s Office sealed the office of Lambda Istanbul LGBTI+ Solidarity Association on Wednesday, as a crackdown continues across the country targeting LGBTQ+ groups.
In a statement, Lambda Istanbul said the move was a further attempt to "isolate LGBTI+ individuals, deprive them of their living spaces, and restrict their freedom to organise".
Lambda Istanbul was founded in 1993 out of an attempt by LGBTQ+ activists to stage the city's first Pride parade. Its office was opened in 2002 and it was formally registered as an association in 2006.
"We do not accept the attempt to frame our association’s activities – which we have conducted openly, transparently, and in compliance with official records for years – as the 'operation of an unauthorised social club', nor do we accept the encroachment upon our living spaces!" the group said in its statement.
Another organisation, Hevi LGBTI+, also announced on Thursday that their termination had been requested in an indictment prepared by the Istanbul Chief Public Prosecutor's Office.
The group also said the indictment was seeking to prosecute five founding members of Hevi over violation of the law on associations.
Crackdown continues
Homosexuality is not illegal in Turkey, and social attitudes vary, but the ruling Justice and Development Party (AKP) has increasingly targeted the LGBTQ+ community in recent years.

data.title: Middle East Eye: 10 Palestinians killed since dawn
data.author: Katherine Hearst
data.summary:
10 Palestinians killed since dawn
Al Jazeera reports that 10 people have been killed in Israeli attacks across Gaza since dawn, including two strikes on hospitals which killed at least seven people.
A deadly overnight strike on the Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis killed six people, including surgeons and patients, while at least one death was reported after a separate attack near the entrance to Gaza City's al-Shifa Hospital.
Al Jazeera said that multiple casualties were also reported after an Israeli drone struck a vehicle south of Deir al-Balah in central Gaza.
Meanwhile, Wafa news agency reports three deaths following the initial six in the Nasser Hospital attack.
According to the report, Hossam Ali Saleha was killed in a strike targeting a vehicle outside the entrance to al-Shifa Hospital in Gaza City.
In Deir al-Balah, an Israeli drone struck a vehicle in the city's south, killing 26-year-old Nashat Fouad Awwad.
In northern Gaza, another Palestinian was killed and several others wounded by Israeli fire targeting a group of people near Jabalia al-Nazla Cemetery.

Dutch foreign minister declines to deny talks are under way on curbing ICC powers
Submitted by
Sondos Asem
on
Thu, 11/12/2026 - 14:07
MPs asked minister if Netherlands is discussing restrictions that could shield Israeli and US officials from prosecution
The Netherlands' Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen at the Nato foreign ministers' meeting in Helsingborg, Sweden on 22 May 2026 (Jonathan Nackstrand/AFP)
Off
Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen has declined to rule out the suggestion that discussions are taking place over sweeping restrictions on the International Criminal Court (ICC), following a report that the Netherlands is negotiating with Washington over changes that could severely undermine the court's powers.
Questioned in parliament on Wednesday, Berendsen said diplomatic discussions were taking place but he would not specify whether proposals to shield national leaders and restrict the court's jurisdiction were under consideration.
The exchange followed a report by Dutch rights organisation The Rights Forum, citing anonymous diplomatic sources in New York, that the Netherlands was negotiating restrictions in response to US sanctions.
Hanneke van der Werf MP, from the Democrats 66 party, asked whether discussions included immunity for heads of state and government, excluding nationals of countries outside the court's founding treaty from its jurisdiction, and weakening its ability to intervene when national authorities fail to prosecute.
Berendsen's answers did not confirm the reported proposals, but nor did they answer whether the government would reject them.
He told parliament he would send MPs a letter next week setting out the Netherlands’ position for the upcoming Assembly of States Parties, including its diplomatic approach to addressing US sanctions against the court.
"Discussions are currently taking place about the diplomatic track being pursued," Berendsen said.
"I cannot anticipate which subjects are or are not on the table."

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israel says it will ban French left-wing leader Melenchon from entry
data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
Israel says it will ban French left-wing leader Melenchon from entry
Israel said that it would ban French left-wing presidential contender Jean-Luc Melenchon from visiting after he vowed that French vessels would accompany activists hoping to force aid into Gaza if he were elected.
In a statement on Thursday, the Israeli foreign ministry said that it "will not allow individuals who act against Israel" to enter the country.

data.title: Middle East Eye: X suspends campaign account of Palestinian American running for US Senate
data.author: MEE staff
data.summary:
X suspends campaign account of Palestinian American running for US Senate
Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Thu, 11/12/2026 - 18:00
Gaza-born and Philadelphia-based Ahmed Moor launched his challenge against hardline pro-Israel Senator John Fetterman this week
Ahmed Moor, who is running for a Pennsylvania seat in the US Senate in 2028, is pictured in a undated photo from his campaign website (MoorForSenate.com)
Off
A Palestinian American who launched his bid for a Senate seat to represent Pennsylvania in the 2028 election has had his campaign account suspended by the social media platform X.
The account, @moorforpa, belongs to Gaza-born, Philadelphia-raised Ahmed Moor, who said this week he wants to topple hardline pro-Israel Senator John Fetterman when he's up for re-election in two years.
Fetterman has not announced whether he plans to run again.
"FRIENDS! It's official! We're a threat," Moor wrote on his personal X account on Wednesday. "They've suspended the campaign account. Help us maintain the momentum by retweeting and please consider donating."
The campaign account had over 33,000 followers within some 72 hours of its launch.
Middle East Eye has reached out to Moor's campaign.
X no longer maintains an active email account for press inquiries.
'The dignity agenda'
Much in the same way progressives ran their campaigns around the country and successfully carried their districts in the midterm elections on 3 November, leading to historic breakthroughs, Moor's campaign tagline is "Stop Funding Wars. Start Funding Pennsylvania."
"I’m running to end the war in Iran and to promote the dignity agenda: free healthcare, free childcare, and affordable housing," he wrote on X on Monday, when he announced his run.

data.title: Middle East Eye: US House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries wants 'dramatic change' in Middle East
data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
US House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries wants 'dramatic change' in Middle East
US House of Representatives Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries called on Thursday for "dramatic change" in the Middle East and reiterated his support for a two-state solution for Israelis and the Palestinians.
The Democrats' sweeping victories in last week's midterm elections could lead to the curbing of US support for its close ally Israel, putting the spotlight on party leaders' views as they prepare to take control of both houses of Congress on 3 January.
Jeffries, a New York Democrat, is expected to be the next House speaker.
"The status quo is unacceptable, and we need dramatic change. And that looks like, as far as I'm concerned, making sure you have a safe and secure Israel, living side by side as a Jewish and democratic state with an independent Palestinian state that provides dignity and self-determination for the Palestinians," he said at a weekly press conference.
